summary: Portable Xclipse backend core behind the sgpu_abi.c dispatcher, tested against a software fake under ASan/UBSan and TSan with mutation testing, and compiled as an ARM64 Mach-O object with the native kernel argv. No GPU, device, QEMU or real ops implementation was involved.

equivalent_mutants_not_run.reason: Pending work requires a GPU mapping at submit and GPU unmap is refused in flight, so pending implies gpu_maps > 0. Covered by the combined mutant above.
A smaller offset wraps the unsigned subtraction past any possible mapping size, which is at most 128 MiB, so the following clause already rejects it.

lease.note: Self-issued by the Claude session acting as coordinator under the owner directive of 2026-11-10, not by the Codex root coordinator.

review.first: Source-only review of the core by a same-session subagent. Found 7 defects and 2 ops-contract gaps that the mutation suite could not detect; fixed in 223f172 and 673b637.
review.second: Same subagent, source-only, on diff 2fade54..673b637. Found no new lifetime or memory-safety defect and 2 low-severity issues, fixed in f4ed035.
review.not_reviewed: Commit f4ed035 (in-flight failure propagation and the narrowed isolation claim) has tests and mutants but was not re-reviewed. Neither review was independent of this session.

limitations: Passing says the object-lifetime rules hold against a software fake. It says nothing about any GPU, register behaviour, firmware or Metal.
No implementation of sgpu_be_ops for real hardware exists, and nothing sets profile_verified for real hardware. GPU-007, GPU-008 and GPU-012 remain open.
The ARM64 objects were compiled and inspected, never executed or linked into the kernel.
IB contents are not validated; retirement order and the failed-submit contract are trusted from the future hardware path.
The byte budget isolates clients only if the trusted configuration divides it; only table quotas are a hard guarantee.
The waiter-blocks-eviction path has no direct test. See Known limits in docs/procedures/gpu-backend/README.md.
